analysis: Both primary units are base-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 5536-6376). The PR changes in this file are documentation only (head ranges 453-473, 3239-3242, 3255-3286); the patch excerpt is truncated and shows a cluster-onboarding stop-count mechanism (ClusterOnboardingStopped, stopsAsked counter, ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked). The supplied base units cover cluster served-speed records, Qwen/Gemma tensor-parallel notes and the pipeline memory-abort protocol, none of which the visible patch edits, so I found no concrete security regression from them. The served-speed file (~/.darkbloom/cluster/served-speed.json) is owner-only and holds request lengths and speeds, no prompts. The documented build-scoped use of records is an integrity control against stale speed data, not an authorization boundary. The pipeline memory-abort marker runs over the keyed, authenticated data plane, so the peer cannot be spoofed. These sections do not touch the T-041 prefix-cache at-rest posture. The Gemma prefix tier is described as the pipeline's memory tier plus the owner's encrypted SSD tier, consistent with T-041. Open questions for integration: (1) the new stop-count control path runs between two Macs (onboarding status reply, ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked, a stop command on either Mac). The authentication and authorization of that cluster control channel, and whether an unauthenticated peer or a local same-UID process could trigger stops (an availability issue), are not in the supplied evidence because the code is not provided. (2) The truncated patch beyond line 473 was not visible. This is a documentation-only change that does not alter threat-model controls. Neither the stop-control authentication nor the truncated patch rises to a finding without code evidence.
